content.text:
I'm fairly sure BaMnO3 (mp-35078) is present. The fit is only partial, though, so my confidence is moderate.

1. **Single-phase fits:** I fitted each of the nine candidates on its own. BaMnO3 was the only one that accounted for the main peaks, giving R = 0.71 at −1.5 % strain. Every other candidate gave R between 0.94 and 1.02. None of them reproduced the strong peaks near 26.4° and 30.8°.
2. **What the BaMnO3 residual shows:** The leftover features are mostly paired: a positive lobe just below a peak and a negative lobe just above it. That shape means the model peaks sit slightly off the observed ones. Each strain value shifts all peaks by the same fraction, so BaMnO3's peak positions don't quite match. The leftovers are not new, separate peaks that would point to a second phase.
3. **Two-phase checks:** I added the two candidates I tried as the most likely second phases. Mn2V2O7 (mp-19142) only lowered R from 0.71 to 0.69, and LiFe3O4 (mp-1176726) to 0.70. Both residuals kept the same paired shape, so neither looks genuinely present. I did not test the other six as second phases. They fit so poorly on their own that adding them seemed unlikely to help.

{"present": ["mp-35078"], "confidence": 0.6, "note": "BaMnO3 is the only candidate that reproduces the main peaks (R 0.71); the leftover residual looks like slightly misplaced BaMnO3 peaks rather than a second phase, and adding Mn2V2O7 or LiFe3O4 barely improves the fit."}
